meta.title: Economics regression tables
meta.tagline: Every regression table of an empirical economics article, one entry per estimated regression: every printed cell with its row type, the link from each standard error to its coefficient, the regressor of interest, and the specification needed to re-run it.
meta.description: One entry per regression column (a (panel, column) pair when a table has panels): outcome, target regressor(s) with the reason they are focal, the full specification (controls itemised, fixed effects, instruments, weights, clustering, sample restrictions stated operationally) and every printed cell with its row type and its coefficient link. Written for the Robustness at Scale study (384 OLS articles from 17 economics journals, 2005–2025). The records are produced OUTSIDE Metalens by an agent pipeline that reads each article and writes one file per table; this preset is the schema they are imported into, not the recipe that made them.

authors.affiliation: University of Basel; University of Copenhagen

evaluated_with.note: the three verification exercises of the Robustness at Scale study

fields.name: table_inventory
fields.label: Table inventory
fields.help: every numbered table of the article, main text and appendices, whether or not it reports regressions — the list the completeness check audits

columns.name: is_regression_table
columns.label: Regression table
columns.help: true when the table reports estimated coefficients from a regression-style model; balance tables count when they report coefficients with standard errors

columns.name: n_columns_estimated
columns.label: Estimated columns
columns.help: distinct regressions the table reports; panels × columns when panels repeat the columns

fields.name: inventory_note
fields.label: Inventory note
fields.help: what the paper reports instead when it has no regression table (figures, text), and anything odd about the inventory

entries.label: Regression column
entries.help: one estimated column of a table that reports regression coefficients; a table with panels that each report their own regressions gives one entry per (panel, column) pair; a table whose rows are outcomes and whose cells each report the coefficient on one regressor gives one entry per outcome row. Summary-statistics, correlation and variable-definition tables are not entries
entries.title: {table_number} {panel} col {column}

fields.name: regression_id
fields.label: Regression id
fields.help: exactly <artid>::<table slug>::<panel or _>::C<column>, as the pipeline writes it: aer_101_6_3::T3::_::C2 is Table 3 column (2) of article aer_101_6_3 without panels; the slug is the table number with punctuation stripped (Table A.1 → TA1); unique across the whole corpus

fields.name: table_number
fields.label: Table
fields.help: as printed: 'Table 3', 'Table A.1'

fields.name: table_title
fields.label: Title
fields.help: the full caption

fields.name: panel
fields.label: Panel
fields.help: the panel label ('A', 'B'); null when the table has no panels

fields.name: column
fields.label: Column
fields.help: the column label exactly as printed: '(2)', 'Women'

fields.name: column_label
fields.label: Column heading
fields.help: the heading above the column when there is one beyond the number ('Log earnings', 'Women')

fields.name: page
fields.label: Page
fields.help: the page the table is printed on, as the paper numbers it; the evidence items carry the PDF page

fields.name: outcome_variable
fields.label: Outcome
fields.help: the dependent variable of this column as the paper names it

fields.name: target_regressors
fields.label: Target regressors
fields.help: the coefficient(s) the column is ABOUT — the treatment, the instrumented regressor, the policy variable; several only when the claim rests on them jointly (a treatment and its interaction); empty when the column has no focal coefficient (balance table, pure first stage) and the notes say so. Named from the paper's text, never guessed from position

columns.name: row_index
columns.label: Row index
columns.help: the row_index of its coefficient cell

columns.name: why
columns.label: Why
columns.help: one sentence on why it is the coefficient of interest, from the paper's text

fields.name: model_type
fields.label: Model
fields.help: the estimator as the paper states it; unknown when it does not say

fields.name: fixed_effects
fields.label: Fixed effects
fields.help: each dimension separately ('firm', 'year', 'state × year')

fields.name: controls
fields.label: Controls
fields.help: every control individually ('age', 'age squared', 'years of schooling'), never 'demographic controls'; dereference 'as in Table 3' and footnotes

fields.name: iv_endogenous
fields.label: Endogenous regressor
fields.help: the instrumented variable; null when not an IV column

fields.name: iv_instruments
fields.label: Instruments
fields.help: the excluded instruments, each separately

fields.name: cluster_level
fields.label: Clustering
fields.help: the level standard errors are clustered at ('state', 'state × year'); null when not clustered or not stated

fields.name: sample_restrictions
fields.label: Sample
fields.help: operational: the rule and the resulting N where the paper states it ('households with income below 150% of the poverty line in the baseline survey; N = 3,412'), not 'the estimation sample'

fields.name: unit_of_observation
fields.label: Unit
fields.help: 'individual-year', 'firm', 'county'

fields.name: outcome_construction
fields.label: Outcome construction
fields.help: how the dependent variable is built from the raw data

fields.name: data_construction_steps
fields.label: Data construction
fields.help: the steps someone with the data would take to build the estimation sample

fields.name: reproduction_notes
fields.label: Reproduction notes
fields.help: anything else someone re-running this column would need

fields.name: notes
fields.label: Notes
fields.help: anything else about this column: parenthesised values are t-statistics, the focal regressor could not be told from the text, …

fields.name: cells
fields.label: Cells
fields.help: every value printed in the column, top to bottom, including controls, the constant and the statistics rows; nothing skipped, reordered, rounded or added

columns.name: row_index
columns.label: Row index
columns.help: 0-based position down the column counting every printed row (standard-error and statistics rows included)

columns.name: col_index
columns.label: Column index
columns.help: 0-based position of this column within the table

columns.name: row_type
columns.label: Row type
columns.help: read the table notes first: parenthesised values are standard errors in most papers but t-statistics or p-values in some

columns.name: raw_text
columns.label: As printed
columns.help: the cell verbatim, stars and parentheses included: '0.94***', '(0.31)', 'Yes'

columns.name: numeric_value
columns.label: Value
columns.help: the number with stars, parentheses, commas and % stripped, sign and every printed digit preserved; null for non-numeric cells

columns.name: refers_to
columns.label: Refers to
columns.help: on an se / t_stat / p_value / ci row: the row_index of the coefficient it belongs to; null on coefficient rows. This link is load-bearing

columns.name: significance_level
columns.label: Significance level
columns.help: 0.1, 0.05 or 0.01 when the table's star legend states it; null otherwise

columns.name: is_string
columns.label: Structural
columns.help: true for non-numeric structural cells ('Yes', 'No', '✓'), e.g. fixed-effect indicator rows — structure, not results

columns.name: statistic_detail
columns.label: Statistic
columns.help: for statistic_other only: what it is ('adjusted R-squared', 'mean of dependent variable', 'number of clusters')

groups.label: Specification
groups.help: outcome, target regressor, model, controls, sample — as the paper states them; the importer sets it from whether the column re-estimated

groups.label: Cells
groups.help: every printed value transcribed with the right row type and the right coefficient link; the importer sets it from the agreement between two independent runs
